niche_preference_profile: This user most often prefers interfaces with strong visual hierarchy, structured card-based grouping, and deliberate emphasis on key actions or status. They frequently like dark navy or deep dark themes with bright cyan, teal, green, blue, or purple accents, but in some contexts also favor light neutral layouts when they feel cleaner and more breathable. They consistently prefer clearer grouping, modular cards, stronger contrast, and more polished rounded components over flat or weakly structured layouts. They also tend to like concise, scannable information presentation, prominent but controlled CTA treatment, and selected states or status signals that are visually explicit. Rounded corners, pill buttons, badges, chips, and layered panels are recurring positive traits.

top_7_criteria.description: Prefers clear hierarchy with obvious emphasis on primary content, actions, summaries, and status through contrast, grouping, and standout sections rather than flat or weakly differentiated layouts.

Prefers high-contrast color systems, most often dark navy/deep dark themes with vivid neon or purple/blue/teal accents, though also responds positively to light neutral palettes when they appear cleaner and softer.
Prefers modular, organized layouts with distinct cards, separated sections, and clear content structure instead of flat lists, weak grouping, or oversized decorative compositions.

Prefers information that is concise, scannable, and efficiently organized, often favoring compact summaries or richer dashboards when they remain clearly structured over verbose or poorly organized content.
Prefers polished UI components with soft or large corner radius, pill-shaped buttons, rounded cards, outlined fields, and generally refined modern component styling.
Prefers balanced spacing and density—either compact or spacious depending on context—but consistently rejects crowding, oversized empty areas, and poor spatial balance.

Prefers primary actions, selected states, badges, chips, and progress/severity indicators to be visually explicit, prominent, and easy to distinguish rather than subtle, text-only, or weakly emphasized.
